results.title: IYC 2026: Youth urged to challenge HIV stigma in Zunheboto
results.description: Morung Express NewsZunheboto | August 12International Youth Day 2026 was observed at Zunheboto Government College on August 12, along with the launch of the 3rd Round of the Intensified IEC Campaign 2026, under the theme “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations.”Speaking on the significance of the day, Hokishe Chophy, District Programme Officer, DISHA, Zunheboto, encouraged young people to speak up, make responsible choices and contribute positively to society.He stressed the importance of equipping youth with accurate knowledge and encouraging them to become responsible messengers of awareness within their communities.Chophy also highlighted the need to address misconceptions surrounding HIV. He stated that HIV does not spread through ordinary social contact such as shaking hands, talking or being around a person living with HIV. He appealed to the public to avoid stigma and discrimination and instead extend support, compassion and acceptance to people living with HIV.He further encouraged individuals to know their HIV status and stressed the importance of HIV testing, correct information and responsible practices. He called upon youth to actively participate in spreading accurate information and dispelling misconceptions surrounding HIV.Addressing the gathering, Dr G Viholi Sema, Chief Medical Officer, Zunheboto, also emphasised the importance of health awareness and dissemination of correct information. She highlighted the need for collective efforts and greater community participation in addressing health-related concerns.The speakers underscored the important role of young people in promoting awareness and positive social change through responsible communication and informed decision-making.The programme was chaired by Assutoli Aye Shenunu, 5th Semester, Department of English, Zunheboto Government College, while the vote of thanks was delivered by Achok Konyak, Assistant Professor, Department of Economics, Zunheboto Government College.

results.title: Four killed, nine injured as vehicle plunges into gorge in Himachal Pradesh's Sirmaur
results.description: At least four people were killed, and nine others were injured when a vehicle carrying them plunged into a gorge near Gatlog in Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh, police said on Wednesday. The accident took place late Tuesday night when the victims were returning from a hospital with the body of a man, who had died of a heart attack after being taken to a hospital in Sangrah, police said.

results.title: Psychology says people often defend decisions they once made even after the reasons disappear
results.description: Psychology suggests that the real challenge is not making decisions we will never regret. It is developing enough psychological flexibility to recognize when an old justification has stopped serving us, and allowing ourselves to choose differently without treating that change as an admission that we were foolish all along.

results.title: Brahmaputra floods in Assam to moderate as hydropower projects rise in Tibet, Arunachal Pradesh: Himanta Biswa Sarma
results.description: In a proactive move, Assam's Chief Minister highlighted the importance of using hydropower projects from Tibet and Arunachal to mitigate flood issues. He mentioned the government's intention to investigate the funds raised by 72 YouTubers for flood relief as well. Prime Minister Modi has promised federal support for rehabilitation efforts following the flood damage assessments. The state is releasing funds to repair anganwadi centres and plans to assist flood-affected namghars.
